new_theorem: In the exact two-distinguisher crossed corridor with Pr(d<b)>2/3 and Pr(a<u)>2/3, the six-word exchange layers obey A/E>2/9, Z/E<1/6, and if d||u then W/E<1/9; hence Z<3A/4, W<A/2 and Pr(d<u)>8/9 in the incomparable-outer case.
structural_reduction: For width <=3 the set of vertices incomparable with both central endpoints is a chain. Thus the exact-two terminal branch either amplifies to an outer incomparable pair of bias >8/9 and exits by span descent/additional distinguisher, or has comparable outer endpoints d<u and leaves a one-dimensional neutral-chain corridor.
partner_application: account02/B19 r13 proves bounded-depth migration on such chain corridors is impossible in general: its P_m family forces first balanced replacement depth asymptotic to (1-sqrt(2/3))m. Therefore the surviving comparable-outer corridor needs a genuinely global charge or counterexample-specific constraints.
